flashsale.topic: Flash Sales redesign — priced-unit resolution, per-country windows, and the sale/price-change split
flashsale.recommendation: The current design's principles are right — never write onto a listing, derive state from the window, scope by campaign tag, landing page is a real category page — but its mechanics are unbuilt: `effectivePrice(basePrice: number, …)` cannot find a base price, and `pricedUnit`, `stacksWithCoupons`, `timezone` and `landingCategoryId` are all stored, edited, audited and read by nothing. The fix is one missing abstraction: a `PricedUnit` adapter (`src/lib/priced-units.ts`) that normalises `RegionalData`, `DiagnosticsServiceOption.pricing` and `TreatmentPlan.pricing` into addressable `PricedUnitRef`s, plus a three-number contract per unit — `listPrice` (compare-at anchor), `standingPrice` (permanent price, row discount already inside), `sellingPrice` (standing price with at most one sale) — so a sale never compounds with a row discount and never touches the marketing anchor. Then replace `pricedUnit` with a unit filter plus sale-level `excludedUnitRefs`, replace the single `startsAt/endsAt/timezone` instant with a per-country resolvable window, and split off a `PriceChange` entity for permanent scheduled changes so a forgotten sale can never become the price. Every resolver returns a discriminated `ResolvedPrice` with a step-by-step explanation and a `revalidateAt`, which is what makes ops answerable and the read path cacheable at the same time.

combos.topic: COMBOS (bundles) for the Valeo Catalogue & CMS — a Listing carrying ComboConfig whose components are PricedUnitRefs into
combos.recommendation: A combo is neither listing-level nor variant-level assembly: it is a LISTING that carries `combo?: ComboConfig`, exactly as Diagnostics and Treatments carry theirs, whose components are `PricedUnitRef { listingId, kind, unitId }` pointing at the row that actually holds money — a variant, a service option, or a plan. Referencing whole listings is impossible (a listing has no price) and variant-level is impossible (a variant cannot address another listing's plan), while making the combo a separate top-level entity would forfeit the URL, the four states, `countryConfig`, tag-based flash-sale scope, SEO locales, price floors and the audit trail that the Listing spine already provides for free. Only `priceMode: "fixed"` stores an amount, in a `ComboPrice` row shaped identically to `DiagnosticsServicePrice`/`TreatmentPlanPrice`; sum-of-parts, percent-off-sum and fixed-off-sum are derived every read, and the compare-at "you save X" figure is always derived so it cannot go stale. freebies.topic: Freebies across listings — mechanism, model, and resolved behaviour for every case
freebies.recommendation: Split freebies by permanence, not by department. If the gift survives after every campaign ends it is a bill-of-materials component of the priced unit — a new `IncludedItem[]` on `ProductVariant`, `TreatmentPlan` and `DiagnosticsServiceOption`, i.e. exactly where price already lives (decision 3). If it has a window it is a campaign, and it becomes a `Freebie` entity that is a sibling of `FlashSale`, never written onto the listing. In both cases the gift is a typed reference `{ listingId, unitKind, unitId?, quantity }` to a real listing at its real price — never a hand-typed string (kills `TreatmentPlan.giftEn`), never a duplicate listing (`pkg-blood-417` "GLP-1 Baseline Blood Test (Free with Wegovy)" vs the canonical `pkg-blood-398`), and never a zero-priced part, because a second price of 0 for a real product leaks into `catalog_pricing`, category price filters and search. This work is blocked on one function that does not exist anywhere in the repo: `pricedUnits(listing, country, cityId?)`, which flash sales also need (`flash-sales/page.tsx:405-407` hardcodes `variants[0]` and `"UAE"`).
